key_insight: The paper proposes an offline-trained, channel-independent QAOA angle dictionary for RIS phase optimization that can transfer across channel models and system sizes without per-instance tuning.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce calibration cost for RIS deployment by using a fixed phase codebook and precomputed QAOA angles, making quantum-assisted beam/power control more practical for future FTQ hardware.
method: Build a $2^M$-phase unit-circle dictionary for RIS phase selection.
Optimize QAOA angles offline using an infinite-size mixed-$q$ Gaussian spin-glass limit.
Evaluate order-2 and order-4 Hamiltonian reductions with analytical and simulation-based studies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical and numerical evaluation up to $N=K\le100$ and QAOA depth $p=9$, with transfer tests on Rayleigh, Rician/LoS, cascaded double-fading, and spatially correlated channels at $N\in\{5,12\}$.
watch_item: The reported advantage is strongest for the order-2 model; the order-4 model underperforms a classical reference, so scalability and hardware feasibility remain uncertain.
paper_title: Offline Channel-Independent QAOA Angles for RIS Power Aggregation: Unit-Circle Phase Dictionaries and Infinite-Size Spin-Glass Limits
